comments.author: @peter-rhodes
comments.text:
This sort of thing is going to put in-house on company's website. How long before twitter just adds that kind of feature, so whenever you go to post this feature pops up and asks you if you want to maximize engagement?

Twitter would be able to internally delay the time for the post to be made (well, it wouldn't be hard for them to add this feature), so there would be no need for autonomous function calling within the model.

This is going to happen across the board. So another example, when you try to sell on ebay or amazon or etsy or whatever this feature will pop-up that asks you if you want AI to refine your post, automate tags for you and post it at an optimal time. Hopefully also, soon, you will be able to just upload ever photo you took of an item and it will be able to automatically choose the best ones and crop them most effectively so you don't have to bother.

Sites like this could add a subscription fee for the service, or just supply it to everyone for free and charge a higher selling fee. But in any case i hope sites get onto this tech fast, and they really should do.

Another idea that may happen soon: When you go to buy anything there will be browser plugins that will automatically scour the internet for the best price, potentially even haggle with sellers for you on your behalf, recommend to potentially wait if it's likely the price will soon be reduced in a sale or whatever. Then finally buy it for you when the price is best, as determined by you that a purchase should be made. Websites would have to allow these kinds of bots in and cater to them, otherwise they'd be losing out too much on all the customers that want to use this kind of thing (which could soon be just about everybody, because why wouldn't you?). They could also maybe even pass on the cost of a user running this bot onto the seller, so a user could check a box that only purchases from sellers that do this. So users could effectively run this bot for free. Sellers would be forced into doing this if they wished to maintain themselves in the market.
